limitations: Accepted as a partial result under the stated correctly specified Gaussian model, deterministic equation-specific full-column-rank designs, and unrestricted positive-definite covariance. The certificate controls every stationary point, not merely a fitted local optimum. The exponential conclusion requires the declared fixed response dimension and covariance spectrum and sublinear union design rank. Conservative constants, small-sample vacuity, and covariance-conditioning dependence remain limitations. The editorial comparison with the cited recent scalar-regressor preprint remains provisional because that primary source was not independently accessible.
claim.scope_statement:
Proves an explicit finite-sample upper bound on failure of uniqueness of every stationary point of the full Gaussian SUR likelihood, with arbitrary deterministic full-column-rank equation-specific matrix designs and unrestricted positive-definite covariance. The unique stationary point on the certified event is a strict global maximum. Failure probability decays exponentially for fixed response dimension and covariance spectrum when union design rank is o(n). Includes a deterministic observed-data sufficient certificate. No optimal exponent, covariance-uniform guarantee, non-Gaussian extension or resolution of every interpretation of the workshop question is asserted.

Significance relative to the checked source: Addresses the original SUR likelihood rate question beyond the checked prior attempt's common-design MANOVA calculation. A checked September 2026 preprint already supplies a scalar-private-regressor bivariate rate and is explicitly credited. The present theorem covers multiple private regressors and arbitrary finite response dimension, with constants depending on covariance conditioning; it is not claimed to dominate that prior bound.
